Fischbach Staff to Hold Mobile Office Hours in Sauk Centre on September 18 | Press Releases | Congresswoman Michelle Fischbach Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Press Press Releases Print Fischbach Staff to Hold Mobile Office Hours in Sauk Centre on September 18 August 24 , 2026 Staff from the Office of Congresswoman Michelle Fischbach will be hold ing mobile office hours in Sauk Centre at the Sauk Centre City Hall (320 Oak St. S) on September 18th, from 11:00 AM to 2:00 PM. The congressional staff will be available to answer constituent questions and take feedback on policy issues. The Congresswoman’s office will also be able to assist constituents with issues such as passport processing, veterans’ needs, tax refunds, Social Security benefits, and connect them with federal agencies like FEMA, FSA, and more. For any questions regarding the mobile office hours, please call the Congresswoman’s office at (202) 225-2165. For more information on Congresswoman Fischbach and her service on behalf of Western Minnesota, please visit fischbach.house.gov. Fischbach Introduces the Hardworking Seniors Act August 14 , 2026 Washington, DC - This week, Congresswoman Michelle Fischbach (MN-07) introduced the Hardworking Seniors Act to allow our seniors to continue contributing to Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) while covered under Medicare Part A.  "Hardworking seniors are currently barred from contributing to tax-advantaged Health Savings Accounts just because they are receiving Medicare," said Rep. Fischbach . "I am excited to introduce the Hardworking Seniors Act to help America's working seniors continue to make these contributions and receive the tax benefits that go with them."   The Hardworking Seniors Act received support from several outside organizations:  A letter of support from the Employers Council on Flexible Compensation (ECFC) stated, "Allowing HSA contributions for working seniors would give them a flexible, tax advantaged tool to prepare for these costs, strengthening the financial security and reducing the long term burden on those with fixed incomes. ECFC supports your introduction of legislation to allow working senior to continue to have access to HSAs."  "Thank you very much for introducing the important, hardworking seniors legislation to allow working seniors of large employers with qualifying High Deductible Health Plans to contribute to a Health Savings Account while on their employer's health plan," said Daniel Perrin, Founder of HSA Coalition. "This is a key step forward to allowing those on public health plans to be eligible for a Health Savings Account." Fischbach Leads Letter Urging EPA to Preserve Access to Critical Crop-Protection Tool July 24 , 2026 WASHINGTON, DC - Representative Michelle Fischbach (MN-07) led a coalition of colleagues in sending a letter to Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin, urging the agency to correct Biden-Era regulatory overreach and restore access to Chlorpyrifos, a vital insecticide relied upon by American farmers. In the letter, lawmakers called on the EPA to restore science-based review processes that recognize Chlorpyrifos as safe for use on crops. "America’s farmers produce the safest and most abundant food in the world, but to keep doing that, they need access to safe, proven crop-protection tools," said Rep. Fischbach. "Food security is national security, and taking away tools from our growers threatens their ability to produce crops efficiently. The EPA must correct past regulatory overreach, follow its own scientific risk modeling, and protect the safe crop-management tools our agriculture community relies on." Key Highlights of the Letter: The EPA's own scientific record and risk modeling support the safe use of Chlorpyrifos. Maintaining domestic agricultural output ensures the United States maintains a resilient food supply. Forcing growers toward alternative pest management options imposes significantly higher costs while providing less effective control against destructive pests. The letter received strong backing from key national agricultural stakeholder groups, including the American Farm Bureau Federation, American Soybean Association, American Sugarbeet Growers Association, National Association of Wheat Growers, and U.S. Beet Sugar Association.
